subject: Music Production
title: Berry Gordy's Motown Machine
description: A 60-second lesson on Berry Gordy's Motown Machine.

hook.text: Berry Gordy borrowed eight hundred dollars and started Motown Records in a Detroit house in 1959.

buildup.text: He built a hit-making system with in-house songwriters, musicians, and a strict quality process.

discovery.text: Every song had to pass a Friday morning meeting where staff voted on which tracks deserved release.

twist.text: Gordy modeled his process on Detroit's auto assembly lines, treating hit songs like products.

climax.text: Motown produced more number-one hits than any other label in the 1960s, crossing racial barriers.

punchline.text: An assembly line approach built the greatest hit factory.

quiz.question: What inspired Berry Gordy's production process at Motown?
